Which of the following are NOT considered as the part of endomembrane system?
A. Mitochondria
B. Endoplasmic reticulum
C. Chloroplasts
D. Golgi complex
E. Peroxisomes

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: The endomembrane system includes: ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles. NOT part of endomembrane system: Mitochondria (A), Chloroplasts (C), and Peroxisomes (E) — these have their own independent membrane systems. So A, C and E are NOT part of the endomembrane system.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: RNA mutates at a faster rate.
Statement II: Viruses having RNA genome and shorter life span mutate and evolve faster.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.solution_text: Both statements are correct. RNA has higher mutation rates than DNA because RNA polymerases lack proofreading activity. RNA viruses (like influenza, HIV) have high mutation rates and shorter generation times, allowing them to evolve rapidly.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Match List - Hormones and Their Source
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II.

List I: A. CCK, B. GIP, C. ANF, D. ADH
List II: I. Kidney, II. Heart, III. Gastric gland, IV. Pancreas
questions.solution_text: CCK (Cholecystokinin, A) = secreted from duodenum/pancreas area (IV - Pancreas/intestine). GIP (Gastric Inhibitory Peptide, B) = secreted from gastric glands (III). ANF (Atrial Natriuretic Factor, C) = secreted from Heart/atria (II). ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone, D) = acts on Kidney (I). So A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A: Endometrium is necessary for implantation of blastocyst.
Reason R: In the absence of fertilization, the corpus luteum degenerates that causes disintegration of endometrium.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.solution_text: A is true: Endometrium is essential for implantation of blastocyst. R is also true: corpus luteum degenerates without fertilization, progesterone levels drop, causing endometrial breakdown (menstruation). However, R does not explain why endometrium is necessary for implantation — they are two separate facts. Hence both true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Match List - Diseases and Causative Organisms
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II.

List I: A. Ringworm, B. Filariasis, C. Malaria, D. Pneumonia
List II: I. Haemophilus influenzae, II. Trichophyton, III. Wuchereria bancrofti, IV. Plasmodium vivax
questions.solution_text: Ringworm (A) = Trichophyton (II, a fungus). Filariasis (B) = Wuchereria bancrofti (III, a nematode). Malaria (C) = Plasmodium vivax (IV, a protozoan). Pneumonia (D) = Haemophilus influenzae/Streptococcus (I). So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Low temperature preserves the enzyme in a temporarily inactive state whereas high temperature destroys enzymatic activity because proteins are denatured by heat.
Statement II: When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.solution_text: Both statements are correct. Statement I: Low temperature preserves enzymes in inactive state (cold storage); high temperature denatures proteins/enzymes. Statement II: Competitive inhibitors structurally resemble the substrate and compete for the active site of the enzyme.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Match List - Organisms and Excretory Organs
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II.

List I: A. Taenia, B. Paramoecium, C. Periplaneta, D. Pheretima
List II: I. Nephridia, II. Contractile vacuole, III. Flame cells, IV. Urecose gland
questions.solution_text: Taenia (tapeworm, A) = Flame cells (III, protonephridia). Paramoecium (B) = Contractile vacuole (II). Periplaneta (cockroach, C) = Urecose gland/Malpighian tubules (IV). Pheretima (earthworm, D) = Nephridia (I). So A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which one of the following techniques does not serve the purpose of early diagnosis of a disease for its early treatment?
questions.solution_text: Serum and urine analysis is a traditional diagnostic tool that does not serve for early diagnosis at the molecular/genetic level. Recombinant DNA technology, PCR, and ELISA are modern techniques used for early, sensitive detection of diseases (including genetic diseases, infections) even before symptoms appear.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II.

List I (Interacting species): A. A Leopard and a Lion in a forest/grassland, B. A Cuckoo laying egg in a Crow's nest, C. Fungi and root of a higher plant in Mycorrhizae, D. A cattle egret and a Cattle in a field
List II (Name of interaction): I. Competition, II. Brood parasitism, III. Mutualism, IV. Commensalism
questions.solution_text: Leopard and Lion (A) = Competition (I, both compete for prey). Cuckoo laying eggs in Crow's nest (B) = Brood parasitism (II). Fungi + plant roots in Mycorrhizae (C) = Mutualism (III, both benefit). Cattle egret and Cattle (D) = Commensalism (IV, egret benefits by eating insects disturbed by cattle; cattle unaffected). So A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Ligaments are dense irregular tissue.
Statement II: Cartilage is a dense regular tissue.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution_text: Both statements are false. Ligaments are dense regular connective tissue (collagen fibres arranged in parallel), not dense irregular. Cartilage is specialized connective tissue (hyaline, elastic, or fibrocartilage), not dense regular tissue.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In prokaryotes, the positively charged DNA is held with some negatively charged proteins in a region called nucleoid.
Statement II: In eukaryotes, the negatively charged DNA is wrapped around the positively charged histone octamer to form nucleosome.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.

questions.solution_text: Statement I is incorrect: In prokaryotes, DNA is negatively charged (not positively charged) and is associated with positively charged proteins (not negatively charged) in the nucleoid region. Statement II is correct: In eukaryotes, negatively charged DNA wraps around positively charged histone octamer (8 histone proteins) to form nucleosomes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II with respect to human eye.

List I: A. Fovea, B. Iris, C. Blind spot, D. Sclera
List II: I. Visible coloured portion of eye that regulates diameter of pupil, II. External layer of eye formed of dense connective tissue, III. Point of greatest visual acuity or resolution, IV. Point where optic nerve leaves the eyeball and photoreceptor cells are absent
questions.solution_text: Fovea (A) = Point of greatest visual acuity (III, highest density of cones). Iris (B) = Visible coloured portion regulating pupil diameter (I). Blind spot (C) = Where optic nerve leaves, no photoreceptors (IV). Sclera (D) = External layer of dense connective tissue (II, white of eye). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Select the correct group/set of Australian Marsupials exhibiting adaptive radiation.

options.text: Mole, Flying squirrel, Tasmanian tiger cat

questions.solution_text: Numbat, Spotted cuscus, and Flying phalanger are all Australian marsupials showing adaptive radiation. Bobcat is a placental mammal (North America). Mole and Flying squirrel are placentals. Lemur is from Madagascar. Option 2 correctly lists only Australian marsupials.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding female reproductive cycle?
A. In non-primate mammals cyclical changes during reproduction are called oestrus cycle.
B. First menstrual cycle begins at puberty and is called menopause.
C. Lack of menstruation may be indicative of pregnancy.
D. Cyclic menstruation extends between menarche and menopause.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
questions.solution_text: A is correct: Non-primate mammals have oestrus cycle. B is incorrect: First menstrual cycle is called menarche (not menopause; menopause is cessation of menstruation). C is correct: Absence of menstruation can indicate pregnancy. D is correct: Menstruation occurs between menarche (first) and menopause (last). So A, C and D are correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Vital capacity of lung is _________.
questions.solution_text: Vital Capacity = IRV + TV + ERV (Inspiratory Reserve Volume + Tidal Volume + Expiratory Reserve Volume). It is the maximum amount of air a person can exhale after a maximum inhalation. Total Lung Capacity = Vital Capacity + RV (Residual Volume).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II.

List I: A. P-wave, B. Q-wave, C. QRS complex, D. T-wave
List II: I. Beginning of systole, II. Repolarisation of ventricles, III. Depolarisation of atria, IV. Depolarisation of ventricles
questions.solution_text: P-wave (A) = Depolarisation of atria (III). Q-wave (B) = Beginning of systole (I, initial ventricular depolarisation). QRS complex (C) = Depolarisation of ventricles (IV). T-wave (D) = Repolarisation of ventricles (II). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A: Amniocentesis for sex determination is one of the strategies of Reproductive and Child Health Care Programme.
Reason R: Ban on amniocentesis checks increasing menace of female foeticide.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.solution_text: A is false: Amniocentesis for sex determination is NOT part of the Reproductive and Child Health Care Programme — in fact it is banned/discouraged for sex determination to prevent female foeticide. R is true: The ban on using amniocentesis for sex determination does check female foeticide. So A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Once the undigested and unabsorbed substances enter the caecum, their backflow is prevented by
questions.solution_text: The Ileo-caecal valve (also called the ileocaecal sphincter) is located at the junction of the ileum and caecum. It prevents backflow of contents from caecum into ileum. Sphincter of Oddi controls bile/pancreatic juice; pyloric sphincter controls food leaving stomach.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II.

List I: A. Gene 'a', B. Gene 'y', C. Gene 'i', D. Gene 'z'
List II: I. β-galactosidase, II. Transacetylase, III. Permease, IV. Repressor protein
questions.solution_text: In lac operon: Gene 'a' (A) = Transacetylase (II). Gene 'y' (B) = Permease (III, for lactose transport). Gene 'i' (C) = Repressor protein (IV). Gene 'z' (D) = β-galactosidase (I, breaks down lactose). So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II.

List I (Cells): A. Peptic cells, B. Goblet cells, C. Oxyntic cells, D. Hepatic cells
List II (Secretion): I. Mucus, II. Bile juice, III. Proenzyme pepsinogen, IV. HCl and intrinsic factor for absorption of vitamin B12
questions.solution_text: Peptic cells/Chief cells (A) = Proenzyme pepsinogen (III). Goblet cells (B) = Mucus (I). Oxyntic cells/Parietal cells (C) = HCl and intrinsic factor for Vit B12 absorption (IV). Hepatic cells/Hepatocytes (D) = Bile juice (II). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following functions is carried out by cytoskeleton in a cell?
questions.solution_text: The cytoskeleton (microtubules, microfilaments, intermediate filaments) is responsible for cell motility, cell shape maintenance, and intracellular organization. Motility includes cell movement and movement of organelles within the cell. Protein synthesis occurs at ribosomes; nuclear division involves spindle fibres (though these are microtubules, the primary function of the cytoskeleton includes motility).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A: Nephrons are of two types: Cortical & Juxta medullary, based on their relative position in cortex and medulla.
Reason R: Juxta medullary nephrons have short loop of Henle whereas, cortical nephrons have longer loop of Henle.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.solution_text: A is true: nephrons are classified as cortical (located in cortex) and juxta medullary (near the cortex-medulla junction). R is false: it's the opposite — juxta medullary nephrons have LONG loops of Henle extending deep into medulla, while cortical nephrons have SHORT loops of Henle.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Electrostatic precipitator is most widely used in thermal power plant
Statement II: Electrostatic precipitator in thermal power plant removes ionising radiations

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

questions.solution_text: Statement I is correct: Electrostatic precipitators are widely used in thermal power plants to remove particulate matter (fly ash) from flue gases. Statement II is incorrect: Electrostatic precipitators remove particulate matter/fly ash, NOT ionising radiations. Ionising radiation is dealt with by different technologies.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Broad palm with single palm crease is visible in a person suffering from-
questions.solution_text: Broad palms with a single transverse palmar crease (simian crease) is a characteristic feature of Down's syndrome (Trisomy 21). Other features include short stature, round face, open mouth, and intellectual disability.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Radial symmetry is NOT found in adults of phylum ______.
questions.solution_text: Hemichordata shows bilateral symmetry, not radial. Ctenophora, Coelenterata (Cnidaria), and Echinodermata (adults) show radial symmetry. Note: Echinodermata larvae are bilaterally symmetrical but adults are radially symmetrical.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In which blood corpuscles, the HIV undergoes replication and produces progeny viruses?
questions.solution_text: HIV specifically infects and replicates within TH cells (T-helper cells / CD4+ T lymphocytes). The virus uses the CD4 receptor on these cells for entry. Progressive destruction of TH cells leads to AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a cloning vector?
questions.solution_text: A Probe is NOT a cloning vector. Probes are single-stranded DNA/RNA sequences used to detect complementary sequences (used in hybridization). BAC (Bacterial Artificial Chromosome), YAC (Yeast Artificial Chromosome), and pBR322 are all cloning vectors used in recombinant DNA technology.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Match List - Growth Types and Age Pyramids
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II.

List I: A. Logistic growth, B. Exponential growth, C. Expanding age pyramid, D. Stable age pyramid
List II: I. Unlimited resource availability condition, II. Limited resource availability condition, III. The percent individuals of pre-reproductive age is largest followed by reproductive and post reproductive age groups, IV. The percent individuals of pre-reproductives and reproductive age group are same
questions.solution_text: Logistic growth (A) = Limited resource availability (II, S-shaped/sigmoid curve). Exponential growth (B) = Unlimited resource availability (I, J-shaped curve). Expanding age pyramid (C) = Pre-reproductive age group is largest (III, growing population). Stable age pyramid (D) = Pre-reproductive and reproductive groups are equal (IV). So A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Select the correct statements with reference to chordates.
A. Presence of a mid-dorsal, solid and double nerve cord.
B. Presence of closed circulatory system.
C. Presence of paired pharyngeal gill slits.
D. Presence of dorsal heart
E. Triploblastic pseudocoelomate animals.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: B is correct: Chordates have a closed circulatory system. C is correct: Chordates have paired pharyngeal gill slits (at least at some stage). A is incorrect: Nerve cord in chordates is dorsal, hollow and single (not solid and double). D is incorrect: Heart is ventral in chordates. E is incorrect: Chordates are triploblastic coelomates (not pseudocoelomates).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The parts of human brain that helps in regulation of sexual behaviour, expression of excitement, pleasure, rage, fear etc. are:
questions.solution_text: The limbic system (amygdala, hippocampus, cingulate gyrus) and hypothalamus regulate emotions, sexual behaviour, motivation, pleasure, fear, and rage. The limbic system is called the 'emotional brain'.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The unique mammalian characteristics are:

options.text: hairs, tympanic membrane and mammary glands
pinna, monocondylic skull and mammary glands

questions.solution_text: Unique mammalian characteristics are: hairs/fur on body, pinna (external ear), and mammary glands (milk-producing). Tympanic membrane is found in reptiles too. Monocondylic skull is found in reptiles and birds (mammals have dicondylic skull). Option 2 correctly lists uniquely mammalian features.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Functions NOT under Thyroid Hormone Control
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are NOT under the control of thyroid hormone?
A. Maintenance of water and electrolyte balance
B. Regulation of basal metabolic rate
C. Normal rhythm of sleep-wake cycle
D. Development of immune system
E. Support the process of RBCs formation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Thyroid hormones control: BMR (B), erythropoiesis/RBC formation (E), water and electrolyte balance (A), and metabolism. C (sleep-wake cycle) is regulated by melatonin from pineal gland, not thyroid. D (immune system development) is regulated by thymosin from thymus, not thyroid. So C and D are NOT under thyroid hormone control.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Select the correct statements.
A. Tetrad formation is seen during Leptotene.
B. During Anaphase, the centromeres split and chromatids separate.
C. Terminalization takes place during Pachytene.
D. Nucleolus, Golgi complex and ER are reformed during Telophase.
E. Crossing over takes place between sister chromatids of homologous chromosome.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: B is correct: During Anaphase (mitosis), centromeres split and chromatids separate to poles. D is correct: During Telophase, nuclear envelope, nucleolus, Golgi complex, and ER reform. A is incorrect: Tetrad formation (synapsis) occurs during Zygotene, not Leptotene. C is incorrect: Terminalization occurs during Diplotene, not Pachytene. E is incorrect: Crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II.

List I: A. Mast cells, B. Inner surface of bronchiole, C. Blood, D. Tubular parts of nephron
List II: I. Ciliated epithelium, II. Areolar connective tissue, III. Cuboidal epithelium, IV. Specialised connective tissue
questions.solution_text: Mast cells (A) = found in Areolar connective tissue (II). Inner surface of bronchiole (B) = lined by Ciliated epithelium (I). Blood (C) = Specialised connective tissue (IV). Tubular parts of nephron (D) = lined by Cuboidal epithelium (III). So A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is characteristic feature of cockroach regarding sexual dimorphism?

options.text: Dark brown body colour and anal cerci

questions.solution_text: Anal styles are present only in male cockroaches (Periplaneta americana) — they are short, thread-like appendages found on the 9th segment of male abdomen. This is a sexually dimorphic feature. Anal cerci are present in both sexes. Sclerites and body colour are not sexually dimorphic features.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the sequence on corresponding coding strand, if the sequence on mRNA formed is as follows 5'AUCGAUCGAUCGAUCGAUCGAUCG AUCG 3'?
questions.solution_text: mRNA sequence: 5'-AUCGAUCG...-3'. The coding strand (non-template/sense strand) has the same sequence as mRNA but with T instead of U, and same polarity (5'→3'). So coding strand = 5'-ATCGATCGATCG...-3'. The template strand would be complementary and antiparallel to mRNA.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
In cockroach, excretion is brought about by-
A. Phallic gland
B. Urecose gland
C. Nephrocytes
D. Fat body
E. Collateral glands

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: In cockroach, excretion involves: B (Urecose glands - store uric acid), C (Nephrocytes - absorb and store waste), and D (Fat body - stores uric acid). Malpighian tubules are the main excretory organs. Phallic glands (A) are accessory reproductive glands. Collateral glands (E) are female reproductive accessory glands. So B, C and D are involved in excretion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: During G0 phase of cell cycle, the cell is metabolically inactive.
Statement II: The centrosome undergoes duplication during S phase of interphase.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

questions.solution_text: Statement I is incorrect: During G0 phase, cells are NOT metabolically inactive — they remain metabolically active but have exited the cell cycle and are not dividing. They carry out their normal cellular functions. Statement II is correct: Centrosomes (centrioles) undergo duplication during S phase of interphase, concurrent with DNA replication.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which one of the following is NOT an advantage of inbreeding?

options.text: It exposes harmful recessive genes but are eliminated by selection.
Elimination of less desirable genes and accumulation of superior genes takes place due to it.
It decreases the productivity of inbred population, after continuous inbreeding.

questions.solution_text: Option 4 is NOT an advantage — it describes a disadvantage (inbreeding depression). Inbreeding INCREASES homozygosity (not decreases as stated in option 1, which is also incorrect). Option 4 correctly identifies a disadvantage: continuous inbreeding leads to inbreeding depression, reducing productivity and fitness. Options 2 and 3 are actual advantages of inbreeding.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?
A. An excessive loss of body fluid from the body switches off osmoreceptors.
B. ADH facilitates water reabsorption to prevent diuresis.
C. ANF causes vasodilation.
D. ADH causes increase in blood pressure.
E. ADH is responsible for decrease in GFR.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: B is correct: ADH (vasopressin) promotes water reabsorption in collecting duct, preventing diuresis. C is correct: ANF (Atrial Natriuretic Factor) causes vasodilation. D is correct: ADH (vasopressin) causes vasoconstriction, increasing blood pressure. A is incorrect: Excessive fluid loss activates (switches ON) osmoreceptors. E is incorrect: ADH does not directly decrease GFR; ANF decreases GFR. So B, C and D are correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding skeletal muscle?
A. Muscle bundles are held together by collagenous connective tissue layer called fascicle.
B. Sarcoplasmic reticulum of muscle fibre is a store house of calcium ions.
C. Striated appearance of skeletal muscle fibre is due to distribution pattern of actin and myosin proteins.
D. M line is considered as functional unit of contraction called sarcomere.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: B is correct: Sarcoplasmic reticulum stores calcium ions released during muscle contraction. C is correct: Striated appearance is due to alternating arrangement of actin (thin) and myosin (thick) filaments creating I-bands and A-bands. A is incorrect: Muscle bundles (fascicles) are held by perimysium; fascicle itself is the bundle. D is incorrect: Sarcomere (functional unit of contraction) extends from Z line to Z line, not M line to M line. M line is the middle of the sarcomere.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?
A. Basophils are most abundant cells of the total WBCs
B. Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin
C. Basophils are involved in inflammatory response
D. Basophils have kidney shaped nucleus
E. Basophils are agranulocytes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: B is correct: Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin, and heparin. C is correct: Basophils are involved in inflammatory and allergic responses. A is incorrect: Neutrophils are most abundant WBCs (60-70%), not basophils (0.5-1%). D is incorrect: Kidney-shaped nucleus is found in monocytes; basophils have bilobed or irregular nucleus. E is incorrect: Basophils are granulocytes (they have granules in cytoplasm).
